author: Mark Manson
description: A vacation, a drink, a new phone all fade fast. While a skill, a marriage, a craft get richer with repetition. Count how much of your week runs on the first list.
title: Why Purpose Always Beats Pleasure

author: Mark Manson
description:
Your brain is constantly editing reality behind your back.
It exaggerates the future to give you hope, softens the past to help you cope, and reframes the present when reality hurts. Sometimes, a little self-deception is how we survive the truth.
title: Why Your Brain Lies to You (To Protect You)

Casanova had more adventures than anyone in recorded history. He escaped an inescapable prison, ran France's first lottery, slept with over 120 women, and met Voltaire, the Pope, and Benjamin Franklin. He also died broke, alone, and forgotten in a small castle in present-day Slovakia. We use his life as the cautionary tale of what Kierkegaard called the aesthetic stage, where novelty becomes an addiction and every open door is another reason to never walk through one. We talk about the paradox of choice, why your brain is hardwired to hoard options even when it costs you, and Mark's own years as a digital nomad who eventually realized that the more he explored, the less satisfied he became.
